routes.description: Establish that evolutionary naturalism supplies defeaters for rational confidence in the cognitive faculties used to affirm naturalism, without requiring proof that a supernatural alternative is true.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalism's account of belief formation leaves no adequate warrant for trusting human cognition about ultimate reality and the objection cannot be answered merely by demanding evidence of the supernatural.

motionBridge.description: Show that a worldview which undermines warrant for the cognition affirming it cannot itself be rationally affirmed.

centralBridges.description: Establish that physical determination, randomness, or causally idle mental states do not by themselves make beliefs responsive to rational grounds or truth.
Establish that selection for survival and reproduction does not ensure reliable cognition when faculties are extended to comprehensive metaphysical conclusions.
Establish that naturalism may be rejected or rational confidence withheld because of internal incoherence without first demonstrating a supernatural realm.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish metaphysical naturalism from scientific method and require a positive defense of the claim that only nature exists.
Test whether naturalism permits any contrary observation to count against it rather than automatically receiving a natural reinterpretation.

routes.description: Defend rational confidence in naturalism through provisional reliance on cognition, evolved capacities for dependable interaction, and publicly testable evidence while assigning the supernatural claimant the burden of demonstrating an addition to the known natural world.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if objective inquiry supplies a workable basis for corrigible confidence in natural conclusions, the evolutionary reliability objection does not establish global defeat, and no verified supernatural exception displaces the natural account.

motionBridge.description: Show that naturalism remains rationally warranted by objective evidence unless its alleged self-defeat is established or a supernatural exception is demonstrated.

centralBridges.description: Account for sufficiently dependable cognition through unavoidable provisional reliance on experience, evolved social capacities, and correction by shared objective inquiry.
Challenge the asserted connections among naturalism, determinism, survival-directed evolution, and the conclusion that rational thought is unwarranted.
Require independent, repeatable, objective verification before adding supernatural entities or causes to the accepted natural world.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish evidence-governed methodological naturalism and acceptance of the known physical world from an unsupported universal negative about every immaterial possibility.
Specify observable conditions that could support supernatural claims and use repeated testing to preserve revisability rather than immunity from contrary evidence.

sections.title: Naturalism's Definition and Burden of Proof
sections.rationale: The dispute over whether naturalism asserts that only nature exists or provisionally accepts the known natural world determines what each side must establish and whether internal critique can resolve the motion.

sections.title: Physical Causation, Determinism, and Rational Agency
sections.rationale: The claimed gap between physical belief production and responsiveness to reasons is a major proposed mechanism of self-defeat, while objections concerning indeterminism, emergence, and rational processes test that inference.

sections.title: Evolutionary Fitness and Truth-Tracking Cognition
sections.rationale: Whether selection for survival can produce faculties reliable enough for abstract worldview judgments is the principal substantive clash identified by the motion and the central evolutionary component of both routes.

sections.title: Objective Evidence, Experience, and Cognitive Correction
sections.rationale: Appeals to testable data, provisional sensory trust, social cooperation, and collaborative checking bear directly on whether naturalism can justify corrigible confidence despite acknowledged cognitive limitations.

sections.title: Falsifiability and Evidence Beyond Nature
sections.rationale: Competing standards for miracles, prophecy, apparent design, and other purported supernatural effects test both naturalism's openness to disconfirmation and whether any alternative has met the proposed evidential threshold.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
moves.proposition: Acceptance of the known physical world does not by itself establish the stronger claim that no immaterial or supernatural reality exists.
moves.attributionBasis: The passage remains within Aron Ra's uninterrupted opening statement after his explicit introduction.

response.rationale: This constructive move distinguishes accepting the known physical world from asserting a universal negative about all immaterial reality.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly establishes a material definitional and burden distinction.

precisionFindings.rationale: The contrast between the known physical world and a universal negative is explicit and consistently scoped.

calibrationFindings.rationale: It makes a limited burden distinction and explicitly leaves an undefined alternative reality uncertain.

charity.alternative: Metaphysical naturalism may affirm that only nature exists, not merely accept presently known nature.
charity.decisiveQualification: That stronger metaphysical formulation would carry a positive burden beyond provisional acceptance of known reality.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The known-world premise coherently blocks inference to the stronger universal negative, with only minor compression about burden allocation.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual distinction is directly illustrated, but no developed account of competing definitions of naturalism is supplied.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it directly supports the method-versus-metaphysics distinction and its burden consequence.

representationalCharity.rationale: The passage recognizes the stronger positive formulation, though it emphasizes burden shifting more than its possible defense.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt expressly contrasts the physical world all parties know with an uncertain and undefined additional reality.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: Metaphysical naturalism claims that only the natural world is real and therefore carries a burden of proof when the debate asks whether naturalism is true.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly transfers the floor to David Wood, whose uninterrupted opening contains this passage.

components.text: Whether the debated position is metaphysical naturalism and therefore asserts that only natural reality exists.
Whether that stronger affirmative metaphysical claim carries a positive burden in this debate.

response.rationale: The reply directly adopts the stronger metaphysical definition and argues that this affirmative position cannot disclaim a burden of proof.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It explicitly contacts both the definitional distinction and the resulting burden question.

precisionFindings.rationale: Metaphysical naturalism, supernaturalism, and the claimed burden are clearly distinguished throughout the passage.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Given the expressly affirmative definition adopted, the claimed positive burden follows at the asserted force.

charity.alternative: The opposing position may be provisional acceptance of known nature rather than denial of every supernatural possibility.
charity.decisiveQualification: The motion's use of naturalism can still reasonably invite defense of metaphysical naturalism as an affirmative worldview.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference from an affirmative exclusivity claim to a burden is sound, though applicability depends on the contested definition.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual contrast supports the claim, but the passage does not independently establish that this definition governs every naturalist position.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it directly advances the metaphysical-burden bridge rather than the motion-level cognitive issue.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply fairly identifies the definitional dispute, although it does not fully resolve which formulation the opponent actually adopts.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt defines supernaturalism as nature plus something else and says a debate over naturalism cannot reasonably reject all burden.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: If beliefs result entirely from physical processes governed by natural laws rather than a commitment to truth, naturalism supplies no basis for trusting those beliefs as rationally truth-responsive.
moves.attributionBasis: The uninterrupted opening statement remains David Wood's, with no moderator or speaker transition.

response.rationale: This constructive move supplies the causal-production premise of the proposed self-defeat argument by contrasting physical causes with truth commitment.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it states a central causal mechanism and the intended epistemic consequence.

precisionFindings.rationale: The causal claim is recoverable, but the passage slides from physical causation to nonresponsiveness to reasons without stating conditions.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Physical realization alone does not establish that reasoning cannot be truth-responsive, so the categorical inference outruns the stated warrant.

charity.alternative: Physical neural processes could implement reasoning whose causal structure is responsive to evidence and valid inference.
charity.decisiveQualification: Calling the substrate mechanical or mindless does not show that the organized process lacks rational sensitivity.

logicalCoherence.rationale: A material bridge is missing between beliefs having physical causes and those beliefs lacking responsiveness to reasons or truth.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Particles, chemistry, and neural firing are named, but no evidence or defended warrant excludes truth-sensitive physical cognition.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly supplies the nonrational-causal-production premise indispensable to the pro route.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move does not address the strongest implementation account and instead treats physical causation as opposed to rational responsiveness.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt describes beliefs as products of particles, chemical reactions, and neurons governed by natural laws rather than truth commitment.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: Natural selection favors survival and reproduction rather than truth, so faculties adapted for practical behavior lack warrant when extended to abstract conclusions in theology, epistemology, ethics, and metaphysics.
moves.attributionBasis: This extended argument remains within David Wood's clearly introduced and uninterrupted opening statement.

response.rationale: This constructive move states the central evolutionary gap between selection for practical fitness and warrant for abstract metaphysical cognition.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it squarely develops the debate's principal evolutionary reliability challenge.

precisionFindings.rationale: The practical-versus-abstract contrast is clear, but the claim of almost no basis is broader than the supplied evolutionary premise.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Selection not directly targeting truth establishes a gap, but does not alone establish near-total absence of reliability or warrant.

charity.alternative: Fitness can often depend on sufficiently accurate representation, with cultural inquiry extending and correcting evolved faculties.
charity.decisiveQualification: Practical truth correlation does not automatically warrant every abstract metaphysical extension.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The fitness-to-truth gap is coherent, but the move leaves a material bridge from nondirect selection to broad abstract unreliability.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Practical examples and a Churchland reference support the concern, but no comparative evidence establishes the broad reliability conclusion.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly develops the fitness-truth bridge at the heart of the motion.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move identifies the decisive limitation on the alternative but gives too little attention to indirect truth tracking and correction.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt contrasts food, combat, and mating functions with theology, epistemology, ethics, and metaphysics, then invokes survival selection.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
moves.proposition: Human social evolution favored empathy, cooperation, trustworthiness, and widening concern, giving selection reasons to preserve dependable social cognition.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly begins Aron Ra's rebuttal, and this passage continues without a speaker change.

components.text: Whether natural selection can favor dependable cognitive and social dispositions rather than only behavior disconnected from truth.
Whether selection for dependable cooperation warrants cognition about abstract or comprehensive worldview questions.

response.rationale: The reply contacts the claim that selection cannot preserve dependability by explaining selection for trustworthy social traits, but it does not bridge to abstract metaphysical reliability.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: This is a partial answer: it contacts practical dependability but leaves the decisive abstract-extension challenge unresolved.

precisionFindings.rationale: The social-selection claim is clear, though its relevance is implicitly limited to interpersonal dependability rather than global cognition.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The selection story plausibly supports cooperative traits, but its generality and connection to cognitive truth remain underqualified.

charity.alternative: The critique concerns abstract metaphysical truth tracking, not whether cooperation and empathy can be adaptive.
charity.decisiveQualification: Reliable social behavior is relevant evidence but does not by itself establish reliable comprehensive cognition.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The selection account coherently explains dependable social traits, but the inference toward broader cognitive reliability remains incomplete.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The passage offers a plausible evolutionary narrative but no specific evidence comparing cooperative selection with abstract truth tracking.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it attacks the fitness-truth challenge, though only through a limited social-cognition mechanism.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply supplies genuine contrary material but omits the opponent's decisive practical-to-abstract scope distinction.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt says dependable, empathetic, trustworthy people were favored across generations while selfish dispositions were selected against.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: Evolutionary explanations of empathy and cooperative herd behavior do not establish that human cognitive faculties reliably discover comprehensive truths about the universe.
moves.attributionBasis: David explicitly summarizes Aron's evolutionary account of ethics, concedes its population-mechanics claims, and identifies the inference he disputes.

components.text: The inference from adaptive empathy and cooperative dependability to reliable discovery of comprehensive truths about the universe.

response.rationale: The reply expressly identifies the scope gap in the social-selection response and states that cooperative herd behavior supplies no warrant for cosmic conclusions.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It explicitly diagnoses the precise inference failure and states its defeating consequence for abstract reliability.

precisionFindings.rationale: The passage consistently distinguishes limited cooperative capacities from grand-worldview and universe-level truth claims.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The nonentailment is well supported, although saying cooperation gives no basis at all understates its possible indirect evidential relevance.

charity.alternative: Social dependability may be one component of generally reliable cognition rather than a complete proof of cosmic truth.
charity.decisiveQualification: That limited contribution still does not entail reliability for comprehensive worldview judgments.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The reply validly denies entailment from cooperative fitness to comprehensive truth, with a bounded overstatement about all evidential contribution.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The cross-species comparison illustrates the gap, but the broader claim about abstract reliability is not empirically developed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly repairs and advances the principal fitness-versus-abstract-truth bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply accurately isolates the limited force of the alternative, with only slight overstatement in calling it no basis at all.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt contrasts herd instinct and animal cooperation with the much stronger claim that humans can discover truths of the universe.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: Evolutionary naturalism supplies potential defeaters for worldview belief through causal determination and mental states that are mere byproducts without a causal role in producing conclusions.
moves.attributionBasis: The same identified speaker develops a connected sequence of naturalism-specific cognitive objections without interruption until shifting to Aron's flat-earth example.

components.text: Whether evolved social dependability answers the concern that mental states may lack a causal role in producing beliefs.
Whether causal determination itself prevents conclusions from being responsive to reasons.

response.rationale: The move develops distinct naturalist defeater mechanisms but does not directly engage the social-selection account selected as its legal opposing target.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It is issue-bearing contrary material, but the decisive demands of the targeted social-selection move remain uncontacted.

precisionFindings.rationale: The train-whistle analogy clearly presents epiphenomenalism, but determinism and naturalism are not consistently separated.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Framed as potential defeaters, the causal-idleness concern fits the illustrative Huxley account without claiming every naturalist accepts it.

charity.alternative: Many naturalists reject epiphenomenalism and treat mental reasoning as causally realized in physical processes.
charity.decisiveQualification: The argument establishes a defeater only for accounts on which rational mental content is causally idle or otherwise disconnected.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Epiphenomenal causal idleness creates a coherent conditional concern, but its connection to naturalism generally is underdeveloped.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The Huxley analogy makes the mechanism intelligible, but representative acceptance and application to the opponent are not established.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it materially develops the nonrational-causal-production bridge through a specific potential mechanism.

representationalCharity.rationale: The conditional force is reasonably preserved, but the passage does not examine non-epiphenomenalist naturalist accounts.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt compares physical processes to a train and mental states to a whistle that exists but plays no causal role.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: A naturalism that reinterprets every conceivable apparent manifestation of God as aliens or another natural cause becomes insulated from contrary evidence.
moves.attributionBasis: David explicitly takes up Aron's good-faith criterion and develops the Dawkins, powerful-alien, Shermer, and Atkins examples as a continuous rebuttal.

components.text: Whether provisional acceptance of the known physical world entails automatic natural reinterpretation of every apparent supernatural event.
Whether evolved social dependability bears on openness to supernatural evidence.

response.rationale: The move raises a relevant falsifiability concern, but attributed hypothetical reinterpretations do not directly answer the earlier definitional or social-selection claims.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It is relevant contrary material about evidential openness, while the primary earlier move's decisive distinction is not contacted.

precisionFindings.rationale: The insulation test is clear, but examples attributed to some naturalists are generalized toward naturalism without a scope qualification.

calibrationFindings.rationale: As a conditional challenge about what would count as evidence, the force is proportionate, though its target population is implicit.

charity.alternative: Natural reinterpretation can reflect comparative inference to the best explanation rather than refusal to consider supernatural evidence.
charity.decisiveQualification: If every possible observation is excluded in advance regardless of pattern, the position would indeed be evidentially insulated.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The conditional falsifiability test is coherent, though moving from cited examples to naturalism generally requires a scope bridge.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Named hypothetical positions illustrate the concern, but the excerpt does not establish that all relevant naturalist accounts are so insulated.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it directly advances the evidential-openness test and nearly exhausts that bridge's immediate demand.

representationalCharity.rationale: The conditional qualification is preserved, but the move gives insufficient attention to comparative standards for rival explanations.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt asks whether any divine appearance would simply be reclassified as aliens or another natural-world cause regardless of evidence.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
moves.proposition: Because both sides accept the known natural world, the person adding a supernatural realm bears the burden of justifying that addition through independent, repeatable, objective verification.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator gives Aron the rebuttal, and Aron directly contrasts the shared natural world with Wood's additional supernatural assumption throughout the window.

components.text: Which party bears a positive burden when both accept the known natural world and one adds supernatural reality.
Whether supernatural evidence would be considered under independent, repeatable, objective verification.

response.rationale: The reply directly contests the proposed allocation by grounding a burden on the additional supernatural claim and supplies an objective-verification criterion.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the burden dispute and a verification standard, though it does not eliminate a separate affirmative naturalist burden.

precisionFindings.rationale: The shared natural world, added supernatural assumption, and evidential burden are expressly and consistently distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The burden on an additional existence claim follows, while the wording is limited to that additional assumption.

charity.alternative: The debate may require naturalism to defend its own affirmative metaphysical exclusivity independently of supernaturalism.
charity.decisiveQualification: That does not remove the distinct burden on anyone affirmatively adding a supernatural realm.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The shared-baseline and added-claim reasoning is coherent, with only a minor gap if treated as eliminating all naturalist burden.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The burden principle and objective standard are clearly stated but not defended through specific examples of adequate verification.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly advances the supernatural-evidential-burden bridge central to the con route.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply fairly preserves a burden for the additional claim, though it does not fully acknowledge that burdens may be concurrent.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt says both sides accept the natural world and requires justification for the additional supernatural assumption through verification.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: A person's skeptical experiences with failed supernatural claims do not by themselves justify dismissing the wider body of reported miracles, especially if that person's worldview raises doubts about cognitive reliability.
moves.attributionBasis: David takes over after Aron's short reply and directly contrasts Aron's experiences with other reported experiences before returning to the cognitive-reliability objection.

components.text: Whether one person's failed encounters with supernatural claims establish that the broader class lacks objective support.
Whether the naturalist account itself warrants confidence in personal skeptical judgments.

response.rationale: The reply contacts the evidential generalization from personal failures and reconnects it to the disputed reliability of the evaluator's cognition.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts a material evidential component, but does not answer the demand for actual independent documentation of miracles.

precisionFindings.rationale: The limited-scope objection is recoverable, but reported experiences, miracles, and personal cognition are treated too broadly.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Personal failures plainly do not survey everything, but the omniscience rhetoric overstates what the opposing evidential position requires.

charity.alternative: Repeated failed tests can justify provisional skepticism without asserting knowledge of every alleged supernatural event.
charity.decisiveQualification: Such skepticism remains defeasible and does not itself evaluate unexamined documented cases.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The limited-sample point is valid, but the move conflates provisional generalization with a universal dismissal and adds circular reliability rhetoric.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: No wider miracle evidence is actually presented in the excerpt, so the conclusion rests on asserted reports and possibility.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it attacks operational cognitive reliability and the scope of objective skeptical inference, albeit incompletely.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply identifies limited sampling but materially weakens provisional skepticism into a claim resembling omniscience.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt challenges extrapolation from Aron's experiences to everyone else's reports and invokes the naturalist reliability objection against that extrapolation.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
moves.proposition: Repeated objective failure of supernatural claims, together with explicit conditions that would change his mind, supports naturalism without claiming omniscience or insulating it from evidence.
moves.attributionBasis: Aron expressly denies David's characterization and gives a continuous first-person account of failed verification and his evidential conditions through the end of the core.

components.text: Whether the skeptical position claims universal knowledge or instead rests on repeated, publicly corroborated failures.
Whether the naturalist states conditions under which supernatural evidence could change the conclusion.

response.rationale: The reply denies omniscience, grounds its conclusion in repeated objective experience, and identifies verification as a condition that would alter the position.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It directly contacts both the scope accusation and the evidential-insulation challenge, though supporting cases remain generalized.

precisionFindings.rationale: Past confirmed experience, absence of verification, and the conditional willingness to revise are clearly distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The provisional inference is calibrated, though 'never' verified is broader than the excerpt's unspecified body of tests can establish.

charity.alternative: There may be unexamined or disputed supernatural cases beyond the speaker's prior failed investigations.
charity.decisiveQualification: That possibility does not defeat provisional reliance on repeated failures while credible documentation remains available for examination.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Repeated failure plus explicit revisability coherently supports provisional confidence without entailing certainty or evidential immunity.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The passage invokes corroborated past experience but supplies no representative cases, methods, or base-rate comparison within the excerpt.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the motion tier, it directly supports provisional evidential warrant and answers a major insulation objection.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply preserves revisability and avoids the universal-knowledge characterization, with only a broad empirical generalization remaining.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt appeals to objective past experience confirmed by others, denies verified supernatural demonstration, and allows that verification would matter.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: Naturalism can be rejected or rational confidence withheld without proving supernaturalism if its own account of nonrational causes and survival-oriented cognition makes affirmation internally incoherent.
moves.attributionBasis: Wood explicitly identifies his philosophical response, defines metaphysical naturalism, and develops the omnipotent-deceiver and cognitive-faculty analogies.

components.text: The inference that naturalism cannot be rejected or confidence withheld unless a supernatural alternative is first demonstrated.
Whether repeated failures of supernatural claims answer an internal cognitive-reliability critique of naturalism.

response.rationale: The reply expressly separates internal defeat from proving an alternative and states that supernatural disconfirmation does not resolve naturalism's alleged self-undermining account.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It identifies the burden-demand failure and clearly states why the internal critique can proceed independently.

precisionFindings.rationale: The internal-defeat structure is clear, but the claim that evolved faculties have no business beyond survival is overbroad.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Alternative proof is not logically required for internal critique, but categorical cognitive incapacity is not established by the stated premises.

charity.alternative: Naturalism can use corrigible evidence and indirect truth tracking without claiming faculties were selected specifically for metaphysics.
charity.decisiveQualification: Those resources must answer the alleged internal defeater rather than merely demand proof of supernaturalism.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The independence of internal critique from alternative proof is sound, while the underlying global unreliability premise retains a material gap.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Analogies and named philosophers frame the concern, but no developed support establishes that survival-shaped faculties lack abstract warrant.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the motion tier, it directly states the route-completion consequence: rational affirmation may be withheld on internal grounds.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply fairly identifies the burden mismatch but compresses the strongest naturalist account of correction and indirect reliability.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt says nonrational causes and survival-shaped faculties undermine application to naturalism without requiring establishment of supernaturalism.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
moves.proposition: Humans must provisionally accept sensory experience as reality, while claims of an exception to the natural world still require supporting evidence.
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker invokes Hume's claim that humans have no choice but to trust perception, then restates Aron's two formulations of the evidential burden.

components.text: Whether unavoidable provisional trust in perception supplies a workable starting point despite skeptical possibilities.
Whether an alleged exception beyond the natural world still requires affirmative evidential support.

response.rationale: The reply contacts the practical skeptical demand by invoking unavoidable provisional perception and separately maintains an evidential burden for claimed exceptions.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the operational answer but does not fully rebut the narrower question of warrant for abstract metaphysical inference.

precisionFindings.rationale: Provisional sensory acceptance and the burden for an additional reality are clearly stated as distinct claims.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The unavoidable practical starting point is explicitly provisional and does not claim certainty about all reality.

charity.alternative: The internal-defeat argument questions rational warrant, not whether humans can practically avoid using perception.
charity.decisiveQualification: Unavoidability alone does not establish metaphysical reliability, though it can establish a provisional operational baseline.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The provisional starting point is coherent, but its extension from unavoidable perception to warranted naturalist conclusions remains compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The Humean practical point supports provisional reliance, while no specific correction mechanism or reliability evidence is developed here.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly supports operational cognitive reliability through provisional sensory reliance.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply offers a fair practical answer but only partially addresses the opponent's narrower epistemic challenge.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt accepts the natural world provisionally through perception and repeats that evidence is required for something beyond it.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
moves.proposition: Objective data rather than authorities or personal experiences should govern belief, because personal cognition can be unreliable and therefore requires public verification.
moves.attributionBasis: The first-person account of formerly trusting personal experience and demanding objective verification is characteristic of Aron's stated evidential position throughout the exchange.

components.text: Whether skeptical conclusions rest merely on one person's experiences or on publicly verifiable objective data.
Whether acknowledged personal fallibility can be corrected through objective verification.

response.rationale: The reply directly rejects reliance on personal experience and identifies objective verification as the corrective standard for both speakers' fallibility.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the personal-scope challenge and supplies a replacement evidential method, though the method's operation is only asserted.

precisionFindings.rationale: The data-versus-experience contrast is clear, but calling personal experiences meaningless is broader than the intended evidential priority.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Public verification is appropriately demanded for strong claims, but personal experience is not literally devoid of all evidential value.

charity.alternative: Personal experiences can provide defeasible evidence even when they require independent corroboration.
charity.decisiveQualification: They cannot by themselves provide the public verification needed for contested supernatural conclusions.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Acknowledged self-fallibility coherently motivates public verification, with a bounded overstatement about the worthlessness of experience.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The passage states the corrective standard but provides no concrete data, protocol, or example demonstrating successful correction.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly develops the public-correction component of operational cognitive reliability.

representationalCharity.rationale: The decisive corroboration requirement is sound, though describing all personal experience as meaningless weakens the alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt disclaims authority and personal experience, acknowledges inability to trust oneself, and demands objective verification grounded in data.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: A supernatural event would produce observable natural effects that remain open to competing natural reinterpretations, so identifying supernatural causation depends on evidential patterns rather than a direct measuring device.
moves.attributionBasis: An audience member addresses David, after which Wood answers in the first person and uses a miraculous cancer-healing example before Aron begins disagreeing.

components.text: How a proposed supernatural cause could generate observable evidence within the shared natural world.
Whether supernatural causation can be directly and consistently measured rather than inferred from an evidential pattern.
Whether an apparent healing supplies objective natural effects rather than only subjective experience.

response.rationale: The reply concedes direct measurement difficulty and explains that a supernatural cause would be inferred through observable natural effects such as an apparent healing.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the verification demand with a proposed evidential route, but leaves rival explanations and documentation largely undeveloped.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between an unmeasured supernatural cause and subsequent observable natural effects is consistently maintained.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The speaker explicitly says he does not know how to measure the supernatural and offers healing only as a possible inferential case.

charity.alternative: An unexplained recovery could have an unknown natural cause and would not by itself identify supernatural agency.
charity.decisiveQualification: A sufficiently specific, independently documented pattern could still be evidence requiring comparative causal evaluation.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Inferring an unobserved cause from observable effects is coherent, but the criteria distinguishing supernatural from unknown natural causes remain incomplete.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The cancer-healing case is hypothetical and lacks documentation, controls, base rates, or a defended method of causal discrimination.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the claim that supernatural additions lack any possible objective evidential route.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply acknowledges competing interpretation and appropriately frames supernatural causation as an inference rather than direct measurement.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt concedes no consistent direct measure, then uses miraculous cancer recovery as an observable effect potentially bearing on causation.

moves.speaker: David Wood
moves.proposition: Collaborative checking of measurable cognitive errors does not by itself warrant treating survival-shaped faculties as reliable for naturalistic conclusions that extend beyond verification.
moves.attributionBasis: The response restates the cognitive-faculty argument advanced by David throughout the debate and directly answers the naturalist questioner.

components.text: Whether collaborative checking of measurable errors warrants confidence in conclusions extending beyond direct verification.
Whether provisional sensory reliance answers the evolutionary scope objection for comprehensive naturalism.

response.rationale: The reply accepts limited correction but directly challenges the extension from measurable checks to worldview conclusions allegedly beyond those checks.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the decisive correction-to-metaphysics bridge, though it does not analyze specific indirect verification practices.

precisionFindings.rationale: The measurable-versus-beyond-verification distinction is recoverable, but which naturalist conclusions are unverifiable remains unspecified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move cautiously states that the extension seems inconsistent, proportionate to its undeveloped account of verification limits.

charity.alternative: Scientific and philosophical conclusions can be indirectly constrained by shared evidence without direct verification of every proposition.
charity.decisiveQualification: That indirect constraint still requires a defended bridge from corrected local cognition to comprehensive metaphysical confidence.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The limitation argument coherently identifies a scope gap, though it does not establish that naturalistic conclusions actually lie beyond indirect checking.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move gives a conceptual limitation rather than specific evidence about which cognitive errors are corrected and which conclusions remain insulated.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the correction component of operational cognitive reliability at its crucial extension point.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply preserves the strongest indirect-verification alternative while correctly identifying the missing scope bridge.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt contrasts the acknowledged state and evolutionary origin of cognition with treating those faculties as more reliable than naturalism warrants.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
moves.proposition: A documented apparent healing should be considered rather than dismissed, while prior citation failures justify doubt pending examination of the supporting documentation.
moves.attributionBasis: The answer expresses Aron's evidence-first skepticism and refers to his recurring experience debating creationists and checking their cited papers.

components.text: Whether documentation of an apparent healing would be considered rather than dismissed because of prior naturalist commitments.
Whether contrary documentation can in principle force reconsideration of the naturalist position.

response.rationale: The reply explicitly accepts a duty to consider supporting documentation while explaining that prior citation failures inform, but do not determine, its expectation.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It directly contacts the evidential-openness demand and states both the revision condition and the bounded skeptical prior.

precisionFindings.rationale: Consideration, documentation, prior expectation, and openness to error are all expressly and consistently qualified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The negative expectation is explicitly provisional and paired with willingness to revise upon adequate documentation.

charity.alternative: A documented healing might genuinely conflict with the current natural explanation rather than repeat prior citation failures.
charity.decisiveQualification: The documentation must still be examined for what it establishes and whether it identifies supernatural causation.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Prior skepticism and genuine openness are consistently combined by treating expectation as defeasible upon examination of documentation.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Past citation failures rationally inform a prior, but no representative history or proposed healing documentation is supplied in the excerpt.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it strongly supports disconfirmation openness by stating a concrete evidential condition for reconsideration.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply accurately preserves the live contrary possibility while explaining, without making it dispositive, the prior skeptical expectation.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt rejects automatic dismissal, says documentation would force consideration, and characterizes contrary expectation as defeasible prior experience.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
moves.proposition: The descriptions of determinism and rationality used in the critique do not match the naturalist account being defended, so their alleged incompatibility remains unsupported.
moves.attributionBasis: The first-person response rejects Wood's definitions from the naturalist side and is followed by Wood directly clarifying his determinism claim.

components.text: Whether the critique's descriptions of determinism and rationality apply to the naturalist account actually being defended.
Whether naturalism entails determinism and thereby excludes rational thought.

response.rationale: The reply directly denies the assumed determinism and disputes the stated incompatibility, but offers little affirmative account of rational physical cognition.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts the decisive premises but mostly asserts disagreement rather than explaining their failure in detail.

precisionFindings.rationale: The intended denial is recoverable, but the unfinished wording leaves determinism, rationalism, and naturalism insufficiently distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The speaker expressly limits the claim to personal understanding and says the argument appears to fail rather than claiming decisive refutation.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Denying that naturalism entails determinism is relevant, but the passage supplies no developed reason why causal physical cognition remains rational.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The response relies on stated understanding and disagreement, without evidence, definitions, or an account answering the causal inference.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly challenges key defeater premises, although the attack is substantially underdeveloped.

representationalCharity.rationale: The brief and incomplete passage disputes definitions without developing a sufficiently determinate alternative interpretation to test.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt says the speaker's understanding of determinism and rationality conflicts with Wood's descriptions and denies deterministic reality.
